name: Historic Center and Jewish Ghetto
tagline: Honey-stone lanes over the tufa cliff
description: The medieval core of Pitigliano, where narrow stepped alleys wind past the historic synagogue, kosher wine cellars, and the old Jewish quarter known as La Piccola Gerusalemme. Houses seem to grow directly out of the tufa rock. This is the most atmospheric and most photographed part of town, but also the busiest with day-trippers.
bestFor: history lovers and short stays who want to be steps from everything
pros: Full of local history and culture
cons: Crowded with day-trippers in peak season

name: Piazza della Repubblica and Aqueduct Area
tagline: The town's social hub beside the old aqueduct
description: Centered on Pitigliano's main square and the striking Renaissance aqueduct arches, this area blends everyday town life with sweeping views over the Lente river valley. Cafes, the town hall, and the main passeggiata route are here, making it a practical, sociable base just steps from the historic center.
bestFor: remote workers wanting cafes and daily errands within walking distance
pros: Central for cafes and small shops
Easy walk to both old town and parking
cons: Can get busy with tour groups near the viewpoint
Limited parking right on the square

name: New Town Outside the Walls
description: The newer district spreading beyond the medieval walls toward the main road and cemetery, where most locals actually live day to day. Streets are wider, buildings more modern, and parking far easier than in the historic core, though it lacks the dramatic tufa-cliff scenery of the old town.
bestFor: longer stays needing a car, groceries, and normal apartment living
pros: Closer to supermarket and bus stops
cons: Short walk or drive needed to reach the old town

name: Sorano and Sovana (Nearby Villages)
tagline: Sister tufa towns a short drive away
description: Two Etruscan hill towns a short drive from Pitigliano, each carved from the same tufa ridgeland and linked by the ancient Vie Cave sunken roads. Sorano feels wild and less visited, while Sovana is smaller and elegant with a Romanesque cathedral. Basing yourself here means more solitude and lower costs, at the price of daily driving.
vibe: rural, quiet, off the beaten path
bestFor: those wanting maximum quiet, lower rents, and Etruscan scenery
pros: Very low rents and fewer tourists
Direct access to Vie Cave and countryside
cons: Essentially no services without a car
Very limited dining or shopping locally
